messages.subject: stacking order in geom_bar
parts:
My students are complaining that it is confusing that for bar_charts
that use stacking, the order of the stack seems to be the reverse of
the order of the legend. For example in
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/graphics/9ec03446056c3bb1d89ecc34eac0ddbb.png.
I tried to explain that it does make sense because when you stack, the
first one ends up at the bottom but I have to agree that it works out
a little unfortunate.

Is there a way to override the default stacking-order, so that the
first category ends up on top, etc?

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: stacking order in geom_bar
parts:
On Mon, Aug 15, 2011 at 5:28 PM, Jeroen Ooms <jeroe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> My students are complaining that it is confusing that for bar_charts
> that use stacking, the order of the stack seems to be the reverse of
> the order of the legend. For example in
> http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/graphics/9ec03446056c3bb1d89ecc34eac0ddbb.png.
> I tried to explain that it does make sense because when you stack, the
> first one ends up at the bottom but I have to agree that it works out
> a little unfortunate.
>
> Is there a way to override the default stacking-order, so that the
> first category ends up on top, etc?

You can use the breaks argument to scale_fill_hue, like this:

+ scale_fill_hue(breaks = rev(levels(diamonds$cut)))

Best
Ista
